intro: Jelašnica is a village in the hills east of Niš in southern Serbia, by the gorge of the Jelašnica river. On an open slope nearby stands a pedunculate oak with long, almost level limbs, which a reader photographed and sent to us with their own figures: about 300 years old and, they say, under state protection in a nature reserve. We have not yet found that record, and we would like to.

trees.story:
"300 years old," wrote the reader who sent us this oak from the hills by Jelašnica, east of Niš in southern Serbia. "It's under state protection. In special nature reserve in Jelasnica. Photo by me."

Their photograph shows a pedunculate oak that has had open ground to itself for a long time. The trunk is short and thick, its grey bark broken into deep plates, and only a couple of metres up it opens into great limbs that run out sideways almost level before they climb, the shape an oak takes when no forest crowds it. Behind it stands a second old oak of the same build, and around both the grass of a sunny slope runs down into scrub turning yellow with the season.

The age and the protection are the reader's words, and so is the girth: their tape gave the trunk about 200 centimetres round. We have not yet found the reserve's own record of this tree. If you know it, or have measured the oak yourself, tell us here and we will add it.

Stand under the long limbs and look up through the crown.

question_meta: An open-grown pedunculate oak near Jelašnica, east of Niš in Serbia, sent by a reader: where it stands and what we know so far.
question_answer: The oak stands on an open grassy slope near Cukljenik, by Jelašnica in the Niška Banja municipality of Niš, at the spot where a reader took its photograph. The reader says it lies in a protected nature reserve, so keep to the paths.
question_context: Jelašnica is a village in the hills east of Niš in southern Serbia, on the river of the same name. A reader who walked there sent us a photograph of a pedunculate oak on an open slope, and a short note: about 300 years old, under state protection, in a special nature reserve at Jelašnica. Those are their words; we have not yet found the reserve's own record of this tree. The photograph shows an oak that has grown without a forest around it: a short, thick trunk with grey plated bark, and limbs that leave it a couple of metres up and run out almost level before climbing. A second old oak of the same shape stands just behind. The reader's tape gave the trunk about 200 centimetres round. If you know the tree's record, its age, or the path to it, tell us on its page and we will add it.

faq.q: Where is the oak near Jelašnica?
faq.a: On an open grassy slope near Cukljenik, by Jelašnica, in the Niška Banja municipality east of Niš, Serbia. The pin marks where a reader stood to photograph it.

faq.q: How old is the Jelašnica oak?
faq.a: About 300 years by the estimate of the reader who sent it. We have no register record or measured age yet.
The reader walked up to it on open ground. They say it stands in a protected nature reserve, so keep to the paths.
